USMLE-style practice · Orthopedics

Selecting additional imaging

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 34-year-old cyclist has persistent radial-sided wrist pain after a fall. The examination remains suspicious for a scaphoid fracture, but the first radiographs are unrevealing. Which imaging test can identify an occult fracture before it becomes visible on repeat plain films?

  1. MRI of the wrist
  2. Repeat the identical radiographic views immediately
  3. Stress radiographs of the scapholunate interval
  4. Ultrasound limited to the first dorsal tendon compartment
  5. Radiographs of the opposite wrist alone
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

MRI of the wrist

MRI can reveal a scaphoid fracture that is occult on initial radiographs.

Understanding the options

MRI of the wrist
MRI can reveal a scaphoid fracture that is occult on initial radiographs.
Repeat the identical radiographic views immediately
An immediate identical study can remain negative; it does not provide MRI sensitivity to an occult injury.
Stress radiographs of the scapholunate interval
These assess dynamic ligament instability rather than being the preferred test for an occult scaphoid fracture.
Ultrasound limited to the first dorsal tendon compartment
This evaluates tendons rather than reliably excluding a scaphoid fracture.
Radiographs of the opposite wrist alone
Comparison anatomy cannot establish or exclude an occult fracture in the injured wrist.
